title.zh: 卷一百二十六 周書17: 列傳六 馮道
title.en: Volume 126 Book of Later Zhou 28: Biographies 6 - Feng Dao
title.raw: 卷一百二十六 周書17: 列傳六 馮道 Volume 126 Book of Later Zhou 28: Biographies 6 - Feng Dao

sentences.zh: 馮道，字可道，瀛州景城人。

translations.literal: Feng Dao, styled Kedao, was a native of Jingcheng in Ying Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Feng Dao, courtesy name Kedao, came from Jingcheng in Ying Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 其先為農為儒，不恒其業。

translations.literal: His forebears had been farmers and scholars by turns, without a fixed occupation.
translations.idiomatic: His family had alternated between farming and scholarship, never settling on one calling.

sentences.zh: 道少純厚，好學能文，不恥惡衣食，負米奉親之外，惟以披誦吟諷為事，雖大雪擁戶，凝塵滿席，湛如也。

translations.literal: In youth Dao was pure and earnest, fond of study and skilled in letters, not ashamed of coarse food and clothing; apart from carrying rice to support his parents, he devoted himself solely to reading aloud and reciting poetry. Even when heavy snow blocked the doorway and dust lay thick on the mat, he remained serene.
translations.idiomatic: As a young man Feng Dao was sincere and steady, devoted to learning and adept at writing, and unashamed of plain food and worn clothes. Beyond carrying rice to support his parents, he spent his days reading and chanting verse; even when snow piled against the door and dust coated the floor mats, he remained perfectly at ease.

sentences.zh: 天祐中，劉守光署為幽州掾。

translations.literal: During the Tianyou era, Liu Shouguang appointed him an aide in You Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: In the Tianyou period Liu Shouguang appointed him a staff officer in Youzhou.

sentences.zh: 守光引兵伐中山，訪於僚屬，道常以利害箴之，守光怒，置於獄中，尋為人所救免。

translations.literal: When Shouguang led troops to attack Zhongshan and consulted his staff, Dao often admonished him on advantage and harm. Shouguang grew angry and put him in prison, but he was soon rescued and released by others.
translations.idiomatic: When Shouguang marched against Zhongshan and asked his officials for counsel, Dao repeatedly warned him of the risks and rewards involved. Shouguang flew into a rage and threw him in jail, but others soon secured his release.

sentences.zh: 守光敗，遁歸太原，監軍使張承業辟為本院巡官。

translations.literal: When Shouguang was defeated, Dao fled back to Taiyuan, and the army supervisor Zhang Chengye recruited him as an inspector of the headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: After Shouguang's defeat Dao fled to Taiyuan, where Zhang Chengye, the military overseer, took him on as a headquarters inspector.

sentences.zh: 承業重其文章履行，甚見待遇。

translations.literal: Chengye valued his literary talent and conduct and treated him with great favor.
translations.idiomatic: Chengye prized both his writing and his character and treated him with marked favor.

sentences.zh: 時有周元豹者，善人倫鑒，與道不洽，謂承業曰：「馮生無前程，公不可過用。

translations.literal: At the time there was a Zhou Yuanbao, skilled in judging men's characters, who was not on good terms with Dao. He told Chengye, "Master Feng has no future prospects; you must not employ him too heavily."
translations.idiomatic: There was a man named Zhou Yuanbao, skilled at reading character, who disliked Dao and told Chengye, "Young Feng has no future ahead of him—you must not rely on him too much."

sentences.zh: 」時河東記室盧質聞之曰：「我曾見杜黃裳司空寫真圖，道之狀貌酷類焉，將來必副大用，元豹之言不足信也。

translations.literal: When Lu Zhi, recorder of Hedong, heard this he said, "I once saw the portrait of Minister Du Huangchang; Dao's appearance closely resembles it. He will surely prove fit for great employment in the future—Yuanbao's words are not to be trusted."
translations.idiomatic: Lu Zhi, secretary of the Hedong commandery, overheard and said, "I once saw the portrait of Du Huangchang, former minister of works—Feng Dao looks strikingly like him. He is bound for high office; Yuanbao's judgment cannot be trusted."

sentences.zh: 」承業尋薦為霸府從事，俄署太原掌書記，時莊宗並有河北，文翰甚繁，一以委之。

translations.literal: Chengye soon recommended him as an aide in the princely headquarters, and shortly thereafter he was appointed chief secretary at Taiyuan. At that time Zhuangzong had united Hebei, official correspondence was extremely heavy, and all of it was entrusted to him alone.
translations.idiomatic: Chengye soon recommended him as staff in the heir's headquarters, and before long he was named chief secretary at Taiyuan. With Zhuangzong holding all of Hebei, the paperwork was overwhelming, and he was given sole charge of it.

sentences.zh: 莊宗與梁軍夾河對壘，一日，郭崇韜以諸校伴食數多，主者不辦，請少罷減。

translations.literal: Zhuangzong faced the Liang army across the river. One day Guo Chongtao, noting that the number of officers dining together was too large for the commissary to manage, asked that the meals be somewhat reduced.
translations.idiomatic: Zhuangzong and the Liang forces faced each other across the river. One day Guo Chongtao pointed out that too many junior officers were dining together for the kitchen to supply and asked that the numbers be cut back.

sentences.zh: 莊宗怒曰：「孤為效命者設食都不自由，其河北三鎮，令三軍別擇一人為帥，孤請歸太原以避賢路。

translations.literal: Zhuangzong said angrily, "I cannot even freely provide food for those who risk their lives for me! Let the three Hebei circuits each choose one man as commander from their armies—I shall return to Taiyuan to yield the path to worthier men."
translations.idiomatic: Zhuangzong burst out, "I cannot even decide how to feed the men who die for me! Let each of the three Hebei circuits pick its own commander from the ranks—I will go back to Taiyuan and make way for better men."

sentences.zh: 」遽命道對面草詞，將示其眾。

translations.literal: He immediately ordered Dao to draft a proclamation face to face, intending to display it to the troops.
translations.idiomatic: He at once ordered Dao to draft a proclamation on the spot to read before the army.

sentences.zh: 道執筆久之，莊宗正色促焉，道徐起對曰：「道所掌筆硯，敢不供職。

translations.literal: Dao held the brush a long while. Zhuangzong, with a stern face, urged him on. Dao rose slowly and replied, "The brush and ink I oversee—I would never neglect my duty."
translations.idiomatic: Dao held his brush for a long while. Zhuangzong, scowling, pressed him. Dao rose slowly and said, "The brush is my charge—I would never neglect it."

sentences.zh: 今大王屢集大功，方平南寇，崇韜所諫，未至過當，阻拒之則可，不可以向來之言，喧動群議，敵人若知，謂大王君臣之不和矣。

translations.literal: Now Your Highness has repeatedly achieved great merit and is on the verge of pacifying the southern foe. Chongtao's advice has not gone beyond what is proper; you may refuse it, but you must not let your earlier words stir up widespread debate. If the enemy learns of it, they will say that lord and minister are at odds.
translations.idiomatic: Your Highness has won victory after victory and is about to crush the southern enemy. Chongtao's counsel was hardly excessive—you may turn it down, but you must not let your earlier outburst alarm the whole camp. If the enemy hears of it, they will think ruler and minister are divided.

sentences.zh: 幸熟而思之，則天下幸甚也。

translations.literal: I beg you to consider this carefully—then all under Heaven will be greatly fortunate.
translations.idiomatic: Please think it through carefully—the realm will be the better for it.

sentences.zh: 」俄而崇韜入謝，因道為之解焉，人始重其膽量。

translations.literal: Shortly afterward Chongtao came in to apologize, and Dao interceded on his behalf. From this people first came to respect his courage.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Chongtao came in to apologize, and Dao smoothed things over for him. From that day men began to admire his nerve.

sentences.zh: 莊宗即位鄴宮，除省郎，充翰林學士，自綠衣賜紫。

translations.literal: When Zhuangzong took the throne at the Ye palace, Dao was made a bureau secretary and appointed Hanlin academician, advancing from green robes to purple.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhuangzong assumed the throne at Ye, Dao was made a secretariat officer and Hanlin academician, promoted from junior green to senior purple robes.

sentences.zh: 梁平，遷中書舍人、戶部侍郎。

translations.literal: When Liang was pacified, he was transferred to Secretariat drafter and vice minister of revenue.
translations.idiomatic: After the Liang was subdued he was promoted to Secretariat drafter and vice minister of revenue.

sentences.zh: 丁父憂，持服於景城。

translations.literal: Upon his father's death he observed mourning at Jingcheng.
translations.idiomatic: When his father died he went home to Jingcheng to observe the mourning period.

sentences.zh: （《談苑》：道聞父喪，即徒步見星以行，家人從後持衣囊追及之。）〉

translations.literal: (From the Tan Yuan: On hearing of his father's death, Dao set out on foot, traveling by starlight. His family followed behind with a bag of clothes and caught up with him.)〉
translations.idiomatic: (From the Tan Yuan: As soon as he heard of his father's death, Dao set out on foot, walking by starlight until his family caught up from behind with a bundle of clothes.)〉

sentences.zh: 遇歲儉，所得俸余悉賑於鄉里，道之所居惟蓬茨而已，凡牧宰饋遺，鬥粟匹帛無所受焉。

translations.literal: When the year was lean, he distributed all surplus salary to the villagers. Dao's dwelling was only a thatched hut. Whatever local officials sent as gifts—whether a peck of grain or a bolt of cloth—he never accepted.
translations.idiomatic: In a famine year he gave away every spare coin of his salary to the neighborhood. He lived in nothing but a thatched hut, and refused every gift from local magistrates, whether grain or cloth.

sentences.zh: 時契丹方盛，素聞道名，欲掠而取之，會邊人有備，獲免。

translations.literal: At that time the Khitans were at their height; having long heard of Dao's fame, they wished to seize him, but because the border people were on guard he escaped harm.
translations.idiomatic: The Khitans were then at the height of their power and, having long heard of Dao's reputation, meant to carry him off—but the border communities were prepared, and he was spared.

sentences.zh: 明宗入洛，遽謂近臣安重誨曰：「先帝時馮道郎中何在？

translations.literal: When Mingzong entered Luoyang, he abruptly said to his close minister An Chonghui, "Under the late emperor, where was Bureau Director Feng Dao?"
translations.idiomatic: When Mingzong entered Luoyang, he turned at once to his intimate An Chonghui and asked, "Under the late emperor, where was Bureau Director Feng Dao?"

sentences.zh: 」重誨曰：「近除翰林學士。

translations.literal: " Chonghui said, "He was recently made Hanlin academician."
translations.idiomatic: " Chonghui replied, "He was just appointed Hanlin academician."

sentences.zh: 」明宗曰：「此人朕素諳委，甚好宰相。

translations.literal: " Mingzong said, "This man I have long known and entrusted—he would make an excellent chief minister."
translations.idiomatic: " Mingzong said, "I have long known and trusted this man—he would make an excellent chief minister."

sentences.zh: 」俄拜端明殿學士，端明之號，自道始也。

translations.literal: " Shortly afterward he was appointed academician of the Duanming Hall—the title Duanming began with Dao.
translations.idiomatic: " Before long he was named academician of the Duanming Hall—the very title Duanming began with him.

sentences.zh: 未幾，遷中書侍郎、刑部尚書、平章事。

translations.literal: Before long he was transferred to vice minister of the Secretariat, minister of punishments, and associate chief minister.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward he was promoted to vice minister of the Secretariat, minister of punishments, and associate chief minister.

sentences.zh: 凡孤寒士子，抱才業、素知識者皆與引用；

translations.literal: Every poor scholar with talent and ability whom he had long known, he brought into office;
translations.idiomatic: He advanced every poor scholar of talent he had long known;

sentences.zh: 唐末衣冠，履行浮躁者必抑而鎮之。

translations.literal: while those from the late-Tang gentry whose conduct was frivolous were always suppressed and restrained.
translations.idiomatic: while those scions of late Tang society whose conduct was flighty he always held down and kept in check.

sentences.zh: 有工部侍郎任贊，因班退，與同列戲道於後曰：「若急行，必遺下《兔園冊》。

translations.literal: There was Ren Zan, vice minister of works, who after the court session withdrew and joked behind Dao to his colleagues, saying, "If he walks too fast, he is sure to drop his Hare Garden Primer."
translations.idiomatic: Ren Zan, vice minister of works, once after court dismissed joked behind Dao's back to his colleagues: "Walk too fast and he'll drop his Hare Garden Primer."

sentences.zh: 」道知之，召贊謂曰：「《兔園冊》皆名儒所集，道能諷之，中朝士子止看文場秀句，便為舉業，皆竊取公聊，何淺狹之甚耶！

translations.literal: " Dao learned of this and summoned Zan, saying, "The Hare Garden Primer was compiled by eminent scholars—I can recite it. Yet the scholars at court read only elegant lines from the examination field and take that as their whole preparation for office, all plagiarizing from official formulae—how exceedingly narrow-minded!"
translations.idiomatic: " When Dao heard of it, he summoned Zan and said, "The Hare Garden Primer was compiled by eminent scholars—I can recite it by heart. Yet court scholars read only polished examination couplets and call that their whole training, stealing every phrase from official templates—how miserably shallow!"

sentences.zh: 」贊大愧焉。

translations.literal: " Zan was deeply ashamed.
translations.idiomatic: " Zan was utterly mortified.

sentences.zh: （《歐陽史》云：《兔園策》者，鄉校俚儒教田夫牧子之所誦也。

translations.literal: (The Ouyang History says: The Hare Garden Stratagems is what village-school rustic scholars teach farmers and herdsboys to recite.)
translations.idiomatic: (The Ouyang History says: The Hare Garden Stratagems was what rustic teachers in village schools had farmers' sons and herdsboys memorize.)

sentences.zh: 《北夢瑣言》云：《兔園策》乃徐、庾文體，非鄙樸之談，但家藏一本，人多賤之。

translations.literal: The Beimeng Suoyan says: The Hare Garden Stratagems is in the style of Xu Ling and Yu Xin—not vulgar talk, yet though every household keeps a copy, most men despise it.
translations.idiomatic: The Beimeng Suoyan says: The Hare Garden Stratagems belongs to the polished style of Xu Ling and Yu Xin, not to crude village speech—yet though every home owned a copy, educated men looked down on it.

sentences.zh: 《困學紀聞》云：《兔園策府》三十卷，唐蔣王惲令僚佐杜嗣先仿應科目策，自設問對，引經史為訓註。

translations.literal: The Kunxue Jiwen says: The Hare Garden Stratagems Treasury runs to thirty juan. In Tang, Prince Yun of Jiang ordered his aide Du Sixian to imitate examination policy questions, setting questions and answers himself and citing the classics and histories for commentary.
translations.idiomatic: The Kunxue Jiwen says: The Hare Garden Stratagems Treasury comprises thirty juan. In Tang, Prince Yun of Jiang had his staff officer Du Sixian model civil-service policy questions, framing his own Q&A and glossing them with passages from the classics and histories.

sentences.zh: 惲，太宗子，故用梁王兔園名其書，馮道《兔園策》謂此也。）〉

translations.literal: Yun was a son of Emperor Taizong, so he named the book after the Hare Garden of the Prince of Liang—this is the work Feng Dao called the Hare Garden Stratagems.)〉
translations.idiomatic: Yun was a son of Taizong of Tang, hence the title drawn from the Liang prince's Hare Garden—the Hare Garden Stratagems Feng Dao cited refers to this work.)〉

sentences.zh: 復有梁朝宰臣李琪，每以文章自擅，曾進《賀平中山王都表》云：「復真定之逆賊」。

translations.literal: Moreover there was Li Qi, a minister of Liang, who always prided himself on his writing. Once he submitted a memorial Congratulating the Pacification of Zhongshan and Wang Du, stating, "recovering the rebels of Zhending."
translations.idiomatic: There was also Li Qi, a Liang dynasty minister who fancied himself unrivaled in letters. Once he submitted a memorial congratulating the pacification of Zhongshan and Wang Du, writing that the court had "recovered the rebels of Zhending."

sentences.zh: 道讓琪曰：「昨來收復定州，非真定也。

translations.literal: Dao reproached Qi, saying, "The territory recovered recently was Ding Prefecture, not Zhending."
translations.idiomatic: Dao corrected him: "What was recovered recently was Dingzhou, not Zhending."

sentences.zh: 」琪昧於地理，頓至折角。

translations.literal: " Qi was ignorant of geography and was utterly humiliated.
translations.idiomatic: " Qi knew nothing of geography and was utterly routed in debate.

sentences.zh: 其後百僚上明宗徽號凡三章，道自為之，其文渾然，非流俗之體，舉朝服焉。

translations.literal: Afterward, when the hundred officials presented three drafts of honorific titles for Mingzong, Dao wrote them himself. The prose was seamless, not in the vulgar mode, and the whole court admired it.
translations.idiomatic: Later, when the bureaucracy submitted three drafts of honorific titles for Mingzong, Dao wrote them himself. The language flowed as one piece, far above the common run, and the entire court stood in awe.

sentences.zh: 道尤長於篇詠，秉筆則成，典麗之外，義含古道，必為遠近傳寫，故漸畏其高深，由是班行肅然，無澆漓之態。

translations.literal: Dao excelled especially in verse: with brush in hand, composition came forth. Beyond elegance and splendor, his meaning embodied the ancient Way, and his works were invariably copied and spread far and near—so gradually men feared his profundity, and from this the official ranks grew solemn, without decadent airs.
translations.idiomatic: Dao was above all a master of poetry and prose: take up the brush and the piece was done. Beyond elegance, his meaning carried the weight of antiquity, and everything he wrote was copied and circulated far and wide—so men gradually stood in awe of his depth, and the official ranks grew grave, without a trace of frivolity.

sentences.zh: 繼改門下侍郎、戶部吏部尚書、集賢殿弘文館大學士，加尚書左僕射，封始平郡公。

translations.literal: He was then made vice minister of the Chancellery, minister of revenue and of personnel, grand academician of the Jixian and Hongwen halls, promoted to left vice director of the Department of State Affairs, and enfeoffed as Duke of Shiping Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: He was next made vice minister of the Chancellery, minister of revenue and of personnel, grand academician of the Jixian and Hongwen halls, elevated to left vice director of the Department of State Affairs, and enfeoffed as Duke of Shiping.

sentences.zh: 一日，道因上謁既退，明宗顧謂侍臣曰：「馮道性純儉，頃在德勝寨居一茅庵，與從人同器食，臥則芻槁一束，其心晏如也。

translations.literal: One day, after Dao had come to audience and withdrawn, Mingzong turned to his attendants and said, "Feng Dao's nature is pure and frugal. Not long ago at Desheng Stockade he lived in a thatched hut, ate from the same vessel as his followers, and slept on a single bundle of straw—yet his heart remained perfectly at ease."
translations.idiomatic: One day, after Dao had paid his respects and withdrawn, Mingzong said to his attendants, "Feng Dao is utterly plain and frugal. At Desheng Stockade he once lived in a grass hut, ate from the same bowl as his men, and slept on a single bundle of straw—yet he was perfectly content."

sentences.zh: 及以父憂退歸鄉里，自耕樵采，與農夫雜處，略不以素貴介懷，真士大夫也。

translations.literal: When he withdrew to his home district in mourning for his father, he plowed, cut firewood, and gathered fuel himself, mingling with farmers without the slightest air of former rank—a true gentleman.
translations.idiomatic: When he went home to mourn his father, he plowed his own fields and gathered his own firewood, living among farmers without a trace of former privilege—he was a true gentleman-scholar.

sentences.zh: 」天成、長興中，天下屢稔，朝廷無事。

translations.literal: " During the Tiancheng and Changxing reigns harvests repeatedly blessed the realm, and the court was untroubled.
translations.idiomatic: " In the Tiancheng and Changxing years the realm enjoyed harvest after harvest, and the court had little to trouble it.

sentences.zh: 明宗每禦延英，留道訪以外事，道曰：「陛下以至德承天，天以有年表瑞，更在日慎一日，以答天心。

translations.literal: Whenever Mingzong held court at the Yanying Hall, he kept Dao behind to consult on outside affairs. Dao said, "Your Majesty, with supreme virtue you inherit Heaven's mandate; Heaven in turn shows abundant years as an omen of blessing. You must be more cautious day by day to answer Heaven's heart."
translations.idiomatic: Whenever Mingzong held court in the Yanying Hall, he kept Dao to discuss affairs of state. Dao said, "Your Majesty rules by supreme virtue and Heaven answers with year after year of plenty. You must grow more careful with each passing day—that is how you answer Heaven's favor."

sentences.zh: 臣每記在先皇霸府日，曾奉使中山，徑井陘之險，憂馬有蹶失，不敢怠於銜轡；

translations.literal: I often recall that in the days of the late emperor's princely headquarters, when I was sent on mission to Zhongshan and passed the peril of Jingxing Pass, I feared the horse might stumble and did not dare relax my grip on the reins;
translations.idiomatic: I often remember that in the late emperor's princely days, on a mission to Zhongshan, I took the perilous road through Jingxing Pass and, fearing the horse might stumble, never loosened my grip on the reins;

sentences.zh: 及至平地，則無復持控，果為馬所顛仆，幾至於損。

translations.literal: but once I reached level ground I no longer held control, and indeed the horse threw me—I nearly came to harm.
translations.idiomatic: but once I reached level ground I let go—and the horse threw me. I was nearly killed.

sentences.zh: 臣所陳雖小，可以喻大。

translations.literal: What your servant has stated is small, yet it may illustrate what is great.
translations.idiomatic: What I tell you is a small matter, but it stands for a great one.

sentences.zh: 陛下勿以清晏豐熟，便縱逸樂，兢兢業業，臣之望也。

translations.literal: Your Majesty must not, because the realm is peaceful and the harvest abundant, give yourself to ease and pleasure. To be cautious and diligent—that is your servant's hope.
translations.idiomatic: Do not let peace and plenty lure you into idleness and pleasure. Vigilance and diligence—that is what I ask of you.

sentences.zh: 」明宗深然之。

translations.literal: " Mingzong was deeply convinced.
translations.idiomatic: " Mingzong took his meaning to heart.

sentences.zh: 他日又問道曰：「天下雖熟，百姓得濟否？

translations.literal: Another day he again asked Dao, "Though the realm enjoys harvest, are the common people truly provided for?"
translations.idiomatic: On another day he asked Dao again, "The realm may be at peace, but are the people truly provided for?"

sentences.zh: 」道曰：「穀貴餓農，穀賤傷農，此常理也。

translations.literal: " Dao said, "When grain is costly the farmer starves; when grain is cheap the farmer is ruined—this is the constant rule."
translations.idiomatic: " Dao said, "When grain is dear the farmer starves; when grain is cheap the farmer is ruined—that is an old truth."

sentences.zh: 臣憶得近代有舉子聶夷中《傷田家詩》云：『二月賣新絲，五月糶秋穀。

translations.literal: Your servant recalls that in recent times the examination candidate Nie Yizhong wrote in his Lament for the Farming Family: "In the second month I sell the new silk; in the fifth month I pawn the autumn grain."
translations.idiomatic: I recall a recent examination candidate, Nie Yizhong, who wrote in his Lament for the Farming Family: "In the second month we sell the new silk; in the fifth month we pawn the autumn grain."

sentences.zh: 醫得眼下瘡，剜卻心頭肉。

translations.literal: "To cure the sore before the eyes, I gouge out the flesh of the heart."
translations.idiomatic: "We cure the sore before our eyes by gouging out the flesh of the heart."

sentences.zh: 我願君王心，化作光明燭。

translations.literal: "I wish the ruler's heart might become a bright shining candle."
translations.idiomatic: "I wish the ruler's heart were a bright candle."

sentences.zh: 不照綺羅筵，遍照逃亡屋。

translations.literal: "That shines not on brocade banquets but everywhere on the houses of the destitute."
translations.idiomatic: "That did not light brocade feasts but every hovel of the destitute."

sentences.zh: 』」明宗曰：「此詩甚好。

translations.literal: '" Mingzong said, "This poem is excellent."
translations.idiomatic: '" Mingzong said, "That poem is excellent."

sentences.zh: 」遂命侍臣錄下，每自諷之。

translations.literal: " He then ordered his attendants to copy it down and often recited it himself.
translations.idiomatic: " He had his attendants copy it out and often recited it himself.

sentences.zh: 道之發言簡正，善於裨益，非常人所能及也。

translations.literal: Dao's words were concise and upright, skilled at bringing benefit—beyond what ordinary men could attain.
translations.idiomatic: Dao spoke with brevity and integrity, and his counsel was of real benefit—beyond what most men could offer.

sentences.zh: 時以諸經舛繆，與同列李愚委學官田敏等，取西京鄭覃所刊石經，雕為印版，流布天下，後進賴之。

translations.literal: At that time, because the classics were full of errors, he and his colleague Li Yu entrusted the academic officials Tian Min and others to take the stone classics carved by Zheng Tan in the Western Capital, cut them into printing blocks, and circulate them throughout the realm—later students relied on this.
translations.idiomatic: Because the canonical texts were riddled with errors, he and his colleague Li Yu put the academic official Tian Min and others to work taking the stone classics Zheng Tan had carved in the Western Capital, cutting them into printing blocks, and distributing them across the realm—generations of students afterward owed him a debt.

sentences.zh: 明宗崩，唐末帝嗣位，以道為山陵使，禮畢，出鎮同州，循故事也。

translations.literal: When Mingzong died and the Last Emperor of Tang succeeded, Dao was made commissioner for the imperial tomb. When the rites were finished he was sent out to govern Tong Prefecture, following established precedent.
translations.idiomatic: When Mingzong died and the last Tang emperor took the throne, Dao was appointed commissioner for the imperial tomb. When the rites were complete he was posted to govern Tongzhou, following established precedent.

sentences.zh: 道為政閑淡，獄市無撓。

translations.literal: Dao's governance was easy and restrained; neither prisons nor markets were disturbed.
translations.idiomatic: His rule was easy and light-handed; neither the courts nor the markets were troubled.

sentences.zh: 一日，有上介胡饒，本出軍吏，性粗獷，因事詬道於牙門，左右數報不應。

translations.literal: One day there was a senior aide, Hu Rao, originally a military clerk, coarse and rough by nature, who for some matter reviled Dao at the headquarters gate. His attendants reported this repeatedly, but he did not respond.
translations.idiomatic: One day his senior aide Hu Rao—a former army clerk, rough by nature—abused Dao at the headquarters gate over some matter. Attendants reported it again and again, but Dao paid no heed.

sentences.zh: 道曰：「此必醉耳！

translations.literal: Dao said, "He must be drunk!"
translations.idiomatic: Dao said, "He must be drunk!"

sentences.zh: 」因召入，開尊設食，盡夕而起，無撓慍之色。

translations.literal: " He then summoned him in, opened wine and set out food, and when they rose at evening there was no sign of annoyance.
translations.idiomatic: " He had him brought in, opened wine, and set a meal before him. They rose only at evening, and Dao showed not a trace of anger.

sentences.zh: 未幾，入為司空。

translations.literal: Before long he was recalled to serve as minister of works.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was recalled to the capital as minister of works.

sentences.zh: 及晉祖入洛，以道為首相。

translations.literal: When the Jin founder entered Luoyang, he made Dao chief minister.
translations.idiomatic: When the Jin founder entered Luoyang, he made Dao his chief minister.

sentences.zh: 二年，契丹遣使加徽號於晉祖，晉祖亦獻徽號於契丹，謂道曰：「此行非卿不可。

translations.literal: In the second year the Khitans sent envoys to bestow an honorific title on the Jin founder, and the Jin founder in turn presented an honorific title to the Khitans. He said to Dao, "This mission cannot be entrusted to anyone but you."
translations.idiomatic: In the second year the Khitans sent envoys to bestow an honorific title on the Jin founder, who in turn presented one to the Khitans. He told Dao, "This mission cannot go to anyone but you."

sentences.zh: 」道無難色。

translations.literal: " Dao showed no sign of difficulty.
translations.idiomatic: " Dao did not hesitate.

sentences.zh: 晉祖又曰：「卿官崇德重，不可深入沙漠。

translations.literal: The Jin founder added, "Your office is lofty and your virtue weighty—you must not penetrate deep into the desert."
translations.idiomatic: The Jin founder added, "Your rank is high and your virtue great—you must not go deep into the desert."

sentences.zh: 」道曰：「陛下受北朝恩，臣受陛下恩，何有不可！」

translations.literal: " Dao said, "Your Majesty received favor from the northern court; your servant received favor from Your Majesty—how could there be anything impossible!"
translations.idiomatic: Dao said, "Your Majesty owes the northern court a debt of favor; I owe Your Majesty the same—how could I refuse!"

sentences.zh: （楊內翰《談苑》云：道與諸相歸中書，食訖，外廳堂吏前白道言北使事。

translations.literal: (Hanlin Academician Yang's Tan Yuan says: Dao and the other chief ministers returned to the Secretariat. After they had finished eating, a clerk from the outer hall came forward to inform Dao of the northern envoy matter.)
translations.idiomatic: (Hanlin Academician Yang's Tan Yuan says: Dao and the other chief ministers had returned to the Secretariat and finished their meal when a clerk from the outer hall came forward to inform Dao of the northern envoy mission.)

sentences.zh: 吏人色變手戰，道取紙一幅，署云：「道去。

translations.literal: The clerk's face changed color and his hands trembled. Dao took a sheet of paper and wrote, "Dao goes."
translations.idiomatic: The clerk turned pale and his hands shook. Dao took a sheet of paper and wrote, "Dao goes."

sentences.zh: 」即遣寫敕進，堂吏泣下。

translations.literal: " He at once had an edict drafted and submitted; the hall clerk wept.
translations.idiomatic: " He had an edict drafted and submitted at once, and the hall clerk burst into tears.

sentences.zh: 道遣人語妻子，不復歸家，即日舍都亭驛，不數日北行。

translations.literal: Dao sent word to his wife and children that he would not return home, lodged that same day at the Capital Pavilion relay station, and within a few days set out north.
translations.idiomatic: Dao sent word to his wife and children that he would not be coming home, took lodging that same day at the Capital Pavilion relay station, and within days was marching north.

sentences.zh: 晉祖餞宴，語以家國之故，煩耆德遠使，自酌卮酒賜之，泣下。）〉

translations.literal: The Jin founder gave a farewell banquet, explaining that for the sake of state and family he was troubling an elder of virtue with a distant mission, poured a cup of wine himself and bestowed it on him, and wept.)〉
translations.idiomatic: The Jin founder gave a farewell banquet, spoke of the needs of state and family, and said he was troubling an elder of great virtue with a distant mission; he poured a cup of wine with his own hand, bestowed it on Dao, and wept.)〉

sentences.zh: 及行，將達西樓，契丹主欲郊迎，其臣曰：「天子無迎宰相之禮。

translations.literal: When he set out and was about to reach the Western Tower, the Khitan ruler wished to welcome him in the suburbs, but his ministers said, "The Son of Heaven has no ritual for welcoming a chief minister."
translations.idiomatic: On the journey, as he neared the Western Tower, the Khitan ruler wished to welcome him in the suburbs, but his ministers said, "The Son of Heaven has no protocol for greeting a chief minister in the suburbs."

sentences.zh: 」因止焉，其名動殊俗也如此。

translations.literal: " They therefore stopped him—such was the way his name stirred foreign peoples.
translations.idiomatic: " They dissuaded him—such was the power of his name among foreign peoples.

sentences.zh: （《談苑》云：契丹賜其臣牙笏及臘日賜牛頭者為殊禮，道皆得之，作詩以紀曰：「牛頭偏得賜，象笏更容持。

translations.literal: (The Tan Yuan says: Among the Khitans, bestowing ivory tablets on ministers and giving ox-heads on the La festival day were special honors—Dao received them all and wrote a poem to record it: "The ox-head I alone was granted; the ivory tablet I may also hold.")
translations.idiomatic: (The Tan Yuan says: Among the Khitans, ivory ministerial tablets and ox-heads given on the La festival were marks of special favor—Dao received them all and wrote a poem to commemorate it: "The ox-head alone was granted me; the ivory tablet I may also hold.")

sentences.zh: 」契丹主甚喜，遂潛諭留意，道曰：「南朝為子，北朝為父，兩朝皆為臣，豈有分別哉！

translations.literal: " The Khitan ruler was greatly pleased and then secretly instructed him to keep this in mind. Dao said, "The southern court is son, the northern court is father—both courts are my lords; how could there be any distinction!"
translations.idiomatic: The Khitan ruler was delighted and then quietly urged him to bear this in mind. Dao said, "The southern court is son to the northern, which is father—yet I am subject to both. What difference can there be!"

sentences.zh: 」道在契丹，凡得所賜，悉以市薪炭，征其意，云：「北地苦寒，老年所不堪，當為之備。

translations.literal: " While Dao was among the Khitans, everything he received as gifts he used to buy fuel and charcoal, hinting at his meaning and saying, "The northern land is bitterly cold—what an old man cannot endure must be provided for."
translations.idiomatic: " In Khitan territory, everything he was given he spent on fuel and charcoal, signaling his intent: "The north is bitterly cold—a man of my years cannot endure it without preparation."

sentences.zh: 」若將久留者。

translations.literal: As though he intended to remain long.
translations.idiomatic: As though he meant to stay for good.

sentences.zh: 契丹感其意，乃遣歸，道三上表乞留，固遣乃去，猶更住館中月餘。

translations.literal: The Khitans were moved by his meaning and then sent him back. Dao thrice submitted memorials begging to remain, but they firmly sent him off; he still stayed in the guesthouse more than a month longer.
translations.idiomatic: The Khitans took his meaning and sent him home. Dao submitted three memorials begging to stay, but they insisted he leave—yet he lingered in the guesthouse more than a month longer.

sentences.zh: 既行，所至留駐，凡兩月方出境，左右語道曰：「當北土得生還，恨無羽翼，公獨宿留，何也？

translations.literal: Once he set out, wherever he went he lingered; in all it was two months before he left the border. His attendants said to Dao, "In the northern land, to win one's life back, one regrets having no wings—yet you alone delay. Why?"
translations.idiomatic: Once he set out, he lingered at every stop and was two months crossing the border. His attendants said to him, "In the north, a man who escapes alive wishes he had wings—yet you alone delay. Why?"

sentences.zh: 」道曰：「縱急還，彼以筋腳馬，一夕即追及，亦何可脫，但徐緩即不能測矣。

translations.literal: " Dao said, "Even if we hurry back, they have swift horses and would overtake us in a single night—how could we escape? Only by going slowly can they not guess our intent."
translations.idiomatic: " Dao said, "Even if we hurry, they have swift horses and would overtake us in a night—how could we escape? Go slowly, and they cannot read our intent."

sentences.zh: 」眾乃服。

translations.literal: " The company then admired him.
translations.idiomatic: " His men were convinced.

sentences.zh: 四年二月，始至京師。）〉

translations.literal: In the second month of the fourth year he at last reached the capital.)〉
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of the fourth year he at last reached the capital.)〉

sentences.zh: 及還，朝廷廢樞密使，依唐朝故事，並歸中書，其院印付道，事無巨細，悉以歸之。

translations.literal: When he returned, the court abolished the Bureau of Military Affairs; following Tang precedent, its functions all reverted to the Secretariat, and its seal was handed to Dao—matters great and small were entirely entrusted to him.
translations.idiomatic: On his return the court abolished the Bureau of Military Affairs and, following Tang precedent, returned its powers to the Secretariat. Its seal was handed to Dao, and matters great and small were entrusted entirely to him.

sentences.zh: 尋加司徒、兼侍中，進魯國公。

translations.literal: Shortly afterward he was made minister of education, also appointed palace attendant, and advanced to Duke of Lu.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward he was made minister of education and palace attendant, and advanced to Duke of Lu.

sentences.zh: 晉祖曾以用兵事問道，道曰：陛下歷試諸艱，創成大業，神武睿略，為天下所知，討伐不庭，須從獨斷。

translations.literal: The Jin founder once asked Dao about military affairs. Dao said, "Your Majesty has been tested through every hardship and founded a great enterprise. Your divine martial prowess and wise strategy are known throughout the realm. To punish the recalcitrant, you must act by your sole decision."
translations.idiomatic: The Jin founder once asked Dao about military affairs. Dao said, "Your Majesty has been tested through every hardship and built a great enterprise. Your martial brilliance and strategic wisdom are known throughout the realm. To punish the recalcitrant, you must decide alone."

sentences.zh: 臣本自書生，為陛下在中書，守歷代成規，不敢有一毫之失也。

translations.literal: Your servant was originally a scholar; serving Your Majesty in the Secretariat, I uphold the established rules of successive dynasties and dare not permit a single hair's breadth of error.
translations.idiomatic: I began as a mere scholar. In the Secretariat I uphold the established rules of successive dynasties and dare not permit the slightest lapse.

sentences.zh: 臣在明宗朝，曾以戎事問臣，臣亦以斯言答之。

translations.literal: In the court of Mingzong, when Your Majesty asked your servant about military affairs, your servant also answered with these same words.
translations.idiomatic: In Mingzong's court, when he asked me about military affairs, I gave him the same answer.

sentences.zh: 」晉祖頗可其說。

translations.literal: " The Jin founder greatly approved his statement.
translations.idiomatic: " The Jin founder was much pleased with his answer.

sentences.zh: 道嘗上表求退，晉祖不之覽，先遣鄭王就省，謂曰：「卿來日不出，朕當親行請卿。

translations.literal: Dao once submitted a memorial requesting retirement. The Jin founder did not look at it but first sent the Prince of Zheng to visit him at home, saying, "If you do not come out tomorrow, I shall go in person to invite you."
translations.idiomatic: Dao once submitted a memorial asking to retire. The Jin founder ignored it and first sent the Prince of Zheng to visit him at home, saying, "If you do not come to court tomorrow, I shall come in person to fetch you."

sentences.zh: 」道不得已出焉。

translations.literal: " Dao, unable to refuse, came forth.
translations.idiomatic: Dao had no choice but to return to court.

sentences.zh: 當時寵遇，無與為比。

translations.literal: At that time his favor and treatment had no equal.
translations.idiomatic: At that time no one enjoyed such imperial favor.

sentences.zh: 晉少帝即位，加守太尉，進封燕國公。

translations.literal: When the Jin minor emperor took the throne, [Dao] was made acting grand commandant and advanced to Duke of Yan.
translations.idiomatic: When the Jin minor emperor succeeded, Dao was made acting grand commandant and ennobled as Duke of Yan.

sentences.zh: 道嘗問朝中熟客曰：「道之在政事堂，人有何說？

translations.literal: Dao once asked a familiar guest at court, saying, "What do people say about Dao in the Secretariat?
translations.idiomatic: Once Dao asked a court acquaintance, "What do people say about my service in the Secretariat?

sentences.zh: 」客曰：「是非相半。

translations.literal: " The guest said, "Praise and blame are evenly divided.
translations.idiomatic: " Half praise him, half blame him," the guest replied.

sentences.zh: 」道曰：「凡人同者為是，不同為非，而非道者，十恐有九。

translations.literal: " Dao said, "Among ordinary people, those who agree call it right; those who disagree call it wrong—so those who deem Dao wrong, I fear, are nine in ten.
translations.idiomatic: " Dao said, "Most people call agreement right and disagreement wrong—so I suspect nine out of ten think ill of me.

sentences.zh: 昔仲尼聖人也，猶為叔孫武叔所毀，況道之虛薄者乎！

translations.literal: In antiquity Confucius was a sage, yet he was still slandered by Shusun Wushu—how much more one so hollow and slight as Dao!
translations.idiomatic: Even Confucius, a sage, was maligned by Shusun Wushu—how much more should a man as slight as I expect it!

sentences.zh: 」然道之所持，始終不易。

translations.literal: " Yet what Dao holds to, from beginning to end he does not change.
translations.idiomatic: " Yet what I uphold, I have never changed from first to last.

sentences.zh: 後有人間道於少帝曰：「道好平時宰相，無以濟其艱難，如禪僧不可呼鷹耳！

translations.literal: Later someone told the minor emperor about Dao, saying, "Dao is suited to be a peacetime chancellor and cannot rescue times of hardship—as a Chan monk cannot be called to hawk!
translations.idiomatic: Later someone told the minor emperor, "Dao makes a fine peacetime chancellor but is useless in a crisis—as useless as calling a Chan monk to hunt with hawks!

sentences.zh: 」由是出道為同州節度使。

translations.literal: " Thereupon Dao was sent out as military commissioner of Tongzhou.
translations.idiomatic: " On this account Dao was posted out as military commissioner of Tongzhou.

sentences.zh: 歲餘，移鎮南陽，加中書令。

translations.literal: After more than a year he was transferred to garrison Nanyang and made director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: After a year and more he was reassigned to Nanyang and made director of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 契丹入汴，道自襄、鄧召入，戎王因從容問曰：「天下百姓，如何可救？

translations.literal: When the Khitan entered Bian, Dao was summoned from Xiang and Deng; the barbarian king then asked him at leisure, saying, "How can the common people of the realm be saved?
translations.idiomatic: When the Khitan took Bian, Dao was summoned from Xiang and Deng. The Khitan ruler asked him casually, "How can the people of the empire be saved?

sentences.zh: 」道曰：「此時百姓，佛再出救不得，惟皇帝救得。

translations.literal: " Dao said, "At this moment not even a second coming of the Buddha could save the people—only the Emperor can save them.
translations.idiomatic: " Dao said, "At this hour not even the Buddha reborn could save them—only Your Majesty can.

sentences.zh: 」其後衣冠不至傷夷，皆道與趙延壽陰護之所至也。

translations.literal: " Afterward, scholar-officials were not harmed or displaced—all owing to the secret protection of Dao and Zhao Yanshou.
translations.idiomatic: " Afterward the gentry were spared slaughter and displacement—largely through the quiet protection of Dao and Zhao Yanshou.

sentences.zh: 是歲三月，隨契丹北行，與晉室公卿俱抵常山。

translations.literal: In the third month of that year he followed the Khitan north, and with the Jin court's ministers and grandees together reached Changshan.
translations.idiomatic: That third month he marched north with the Khitan and reached Changshan together with the Jin court's highest officials.

sentences.zh: 俄而比主卒，永康王代統其眾。

translations.literal: Before long the Khitan ruler died, and Prince Yongkang succeeded to command the host.
translations.idiomatic: Soon the Khitan emperor died and Prince Yongkang took command of the army.

sentences.zh: 及北去，留其族嘉裏以據常山。

translations.literal: When they went north, they left their clansman Jiali to hold Changshan.
translations.idiomatic: As they withdrew north, they left a clansman named Jiali to hold Changshan.

sentences.zh: 時漢軍憤激，因共逐出嘉裏，尋復其城。

translations.literal: At that time Han troops were inflamed with rage and together drove out Jiali, soon recovering the city.
translations.idiomatic: Han troops, furious, then drove out Jiali and soon retook the city.

sentences.zh: 道率同列四出按撫，因事從宜，各安其所。

translations.literal: Dao led his colleagues in dispatching the four directions to pacify and reassure; according to each circumstance he acted as appropriate, and each settled where he belonged.
translations.idiomatic: Dao led his colleagues on missions in all directions to reassure the people, adapting policy to local needs until order was restored everywhere.

sentences.zh: 人或推其功，道曰：「儒臣何能為，皆諸將之力也。

translations.literal: When some praised his achievement, Dao said, "What can a Confucian minister do? It is all the generals' merit.
translations.idiomatic: When people praised his role, Dao said, "What can a scholar-minister accomplish? The credit belongs to the generals.

sentences.zh: 」道以德重，人所取則，乃為眾擇諸將之勤宿者，以騎校白再榮權為其帥，軍民由是帖然，道首有力焉。

translations.literal: " Because Dao's virtue was weighty and men took him as their standard, he selected for the multitude the most diligent veteran among the generals and made the cavalry captain Bai Zairong acting commander; army and people were thereby settled, and Dao was foremost in power therein.
translations.idiomatic: " Because his moral authority commanded respect, he had the leaders choose the hardest-working veteran among the generals and made the cavalry captain Bai Zairong acting commander. Army and people then settled down—chiefly through Dao's influence.

sentences.zh: 道在常山，見有中國士女為契丹所俘者，出橐裝以贖之，皆寄於高尼精舍，後相次訪其家以歸之。

translations.literal: While at Changshan, Dao saw Chinese men and women taken captive by the Khitan; he took from his purse funds to redeem them, all lodging them at eminent nuns' refuges, and later in succession sought out their families to return them home.
translations.idiomatic: At Changshan he saw Chinese men and women held captive by the Khitan. He paid from his own funds to ransom them, housed them at reputable nunneries, and later helped each return to family.

sentences.zh: 又，契丹先留道與李崧、和凝及文武官等在常山，是歲閏七月二十九日，契丹有詔追崧，令選朝士十人赴木葉山行事。

translations.literal: Moreover, the Khitan had first left Dao together with Li Song, He Ning, and civil and military officials at Changshan. On the twenty-ninth day of the intercalary seventh month of that year the Khitan issued an edict summoning Song, ordering the selection of ten court scholars to go to Muye Shan on business.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier the Khitan had left Dao, Li Song, He Ning, and other officials at Changshan. On the twenty-ninth of the intercalary seventh month that year an edict recalled Song and required ten court scholars to go to Muye Shan on imperial business.

sentences.zh: 契丹麻答召道等至帳所，欲諭之，崧偶先至，知其意，懼形於色。

translations.literal: The Khitan Moda summoned Dao and the others to the tent quarters intending to instruct them. Song happened to arrive first, perceived their intent, and fear showed on his face.
translations.idiomatic: The Khitan leader Moda summoned Dao and the others to his camp to give them orders. Song arrived first, guessed what was planned, and could not hide his fear.

sentences.zh: 契丹麻答將以明日與朝士齊遣之，崧乃不俟道，與凝先出，既而相遇於帳門之外，因與分手俱歸。

translations.literal: Moda intended on the morrow to send them off together with the court scholars. Song therefore did not wait for Dao but left first with Ning; afterward they met outside the tent gate, and so parted and each returned home.
translations.idiomatic: Moda meant to send them north with the court scholars the next day. Song did not wait for Dao but left early with He Ning. They met Dao outside the tent gate, said farewell, and each went home.

sentences.zh: 俄而李筠等縱火與契丹交鬥，鼓槊相及。

translations.literal: Before long Li Yun and others set fires and fought the Khitan; drums and spears met in clash.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Li Yun and others set fire to the camp and battled the Khitan at close quarters.

sentences.zh: 是日若齊至，與麻答相見，稍或躊躇，則悉為俘矣。

translations.literal: Had they all arrived together that day and met Moda, showing even a moment's hesitation, they would all have been taken captive.
translations.idiomatic: If they had all gone to the tent that day and hesitated even slightly before Moda, they would all have been captured.

sentences.zh: 時論者以道布衣有至行，立公朝有重望，其陰報昭感，多此類也。

translations.literal: Contemporaries held that Dao as a commoner had utmost conduct, and established in the public court had heavy expectation; such hidden recompenses and manifest responses were mostly of this kind.
translations.idiomatic: Later opinion held that Dao had shown supreme integrity as a commoner and carried great weight in public office—and that such covert rewards of merit were typical of his career.

sentences.zh: 及自常山入覲，漢祖嘉之，拜守太師。

translations.literal: When he came from Changshan to present himself at court, the Han founder commended him and appointed him acting grand preceptor.
translations.idiomatic: When he returned from Changshan to court, the Han founder praised him and made him acting grand preceptor.

sentences.zh: （《洛陽搢紳舊聞記》：贈大監張公璨，漢祖即位之初為上黨戎判。

translations.literal: (Records of Old Notables of Luoyang: Director Zhang Gongcan, posthumously ennobled, served at the start of the Han founder's reign as military adjutant judge of Shangdang.
translations.idiomatic: (From Records of Old Notables of Luoyang: Director Zhang Gongcan, posthumously honored, served when the Han founder first took the throne as military adjutant judge of Shangdang.

sentences.zh: 漢祖在北京時，大聚甲兵，禁牛皮不得私貿易及民間盜用之，如有牛死，即時官納其皮，其有犯者甚眾。

translations.literal: When the Han founder was at Beijing he massed armor and troops, forbidding cowhide from private trade and from illicit use among the people; if an ox died, its hide was at once delivered to the government—offenders were very numerous.
translations.idiomatic: While the Han founder was still at Beijing assembling armies, he banned private trade in cowhide and unauthorized civilian use: any dead ox's hide had to be handed to the government at once, and violators were many.

sentences.zh: 及即大位，三司舉行請禁天下牛皮法，與河東時同，天下苦之。

translations.literal: When he took the supreme position, the three departments proposed enforcing a law forbidding cowhide throughout the realm, the same as in Hedong—the realm suffered under it.
translations.idiomatic: After he became emperor, the fiscal offices petitioned to extend the cowhide ban empire-wide, as in Hedong, to the torment of the entire country.

sentences.zh: 會上黨民犯牛皮者二十餘人，獄成，罪俱當死。

translations.literal: It happened that more than twenty people in Shangdang violated the cowhide prohibition; when the cases were complete, all offenses merited death.
translations.idiomatic: More than twenty Shangdang residents were convicted of violating the cowhide ban, and every sentence called for death.

sentences.zh: 大監時為判官，獨執曰：「主上欽明，三司不合如此起請，二十餘人死尚間可，使天下犯者皆銜冤而死乎！

translations.literal: The Director then serving as judge, alone held fast and said, "Our lord is discerning—the three departments ought not petition thus. Twenty-odd deaths might yet be borne, but shall all offenders throughout the realm die bearing wrongful grievance!
translations.idiomatic: Director Zhang, then serving as adjutant judge, alone objected: "Our lord is wise; the fiscal offices should not petition this way. Twenty deaths might be tolerable—but shall every violator in the empire die with a grievance on his lips!

sentences.zh: 且主上在河東，大聚甲兵，須藉牛皮，嚴禁可也，今為天下君，何少牛皮，立法至於此乎！

translations.literal: Moreover, when our lord was in Hedong, gathering armor and troops in great numbers, cowhide was needed and strict prohibition was possible; now that he is lord of all under Heaven, what lack of cowhide is there, that law should reach this extreme!
translations.idiomatic: " When His Majesty was in Hedong assembling armies, cowhide was essential and a strict ban made sense. Now he rules the world—what shortage of cowhide requires a law this harsh!

sentences.zh: 」遂封奏之。

translations.literal: " Thereupon he sealed and submitted the memorial.
translations.idiomatic: " He sealed the memorial and submitted it.

sentences.zh: 時三司使方用事，執政之地，除馮瀛王外皆惡之，曰：「豈有州郡使敢非朝廷詔敕！

translations.literal: At that time the director of the three departments was just wielding power in the seat of government; except for Prince Feng of Ying, all detested him and said, "How can a provincial commissioner dare oppose the court's edict!
translations.idiomatic: The fiscal commissioner then dominated the government. Everyone but Prince Feng of Ying hated Zhang and said, "How dare a provincial official defy an imperial decree!

sentences.zh: 」力言於漢祖。

translations.literal: " They spoke forcefully to the Han founder.
translations.idiomatic: " They pressed the emperor vigorously.

sentences.zh: 漢祖亦怒曰：「昭義一判官，是何敢如此！

translations.literal: The Han founder also grew angry and said, "A single judge of Zhaoyi—what is this daring such as this!
translations.idiomatic: The Han founder fumed, "A mere adjutant judge of Zhaoyi—how dare he do this!

sentences.zh: 其犯牛皮者，依敕俱死。

translations.literal: Those who violated the cowhide [ban], according to the edict shall all die.
translations.idiomatic: " Those convicted of the cowhide offense shall die as the decree commands.

sentences.zh: 大監以非毀詔敕，亦死。

translations.literal: The Director, for denigrating the edict, also dies.
translations.idiomatic: " Director Zhang, for denigrating the decree, shall die as well.

sentences.zh: 」敕未下，獨瀛王非時請見。

translations.literal: " The edict had not yet been issued when Prince Feng of Ying alone requested audience out of season.
translations.idiomatic: " Before the order went out, Prince Feng alone requested an extraordinary audience.

sentences.zh: 漢祖出，瀛王曰：「陛下在河東時，斷牛皮可也，今既有天下，牛皮不合禁。

translations.literal: The Han founder came out; the Prince of Ying said, "When Your Majesty was in Hedong, prohibiting cowhide was acceptable; now that you possess all under Heaven, cowhide ought not be forbidden.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor appeared, Feng said, "Your Majesty could ban cowhide in Hedong, but now that you rule the realm the ban should end.

sentences.zh: 陛下赤子枉死之，亦足為陛下惜。

translations.literal: Your Majesty's infants dying wrongfully—this too is enough to cause Your Majesty regret.
translations.idiomatic: Your innocent subjects would die unjustly—that alone should grieve Your Majesty.

sentences.zh: 昭義判官，以卑位食陛下祿，居陛下官，不惜軀命，敢執而奏之，可賞不可殺。

translations.literal: The judge of Zhaoyi, though in a low station eating Your Majesty's salary and holding Your Majesty's office, did not spare body and life but dared hold fast and memorialize—he should be rewarded, not killed.
translations.idiomatic: That Zhaoyi judge holds a humble post on your salary yet risked his life to remonstrate. He deserves reward, not execution.

sentences.zh: 臣當輔弼之任，使此敕枉害天下人性命，臣不能早奏，使陛下正，臣罪當誅。

translations.literal: Your servant bears the duty of assisting and supporting; to let this edict wrongly harm the lives of the people of the realm—your servant could not memorialize early and cause Your Majesty to correct it; your servant's crime deserves execution.
translations.idiomatic: As your chief minister I should have stopped this decree before it wronged the empire. I failed to remonstrate in time; if Your Majesty is at fault, I deserve death.

sentences.zh: 」稽首再拜。

translations.literal: " He bowed his head and kowtowed twice.
translations.idiomatic: " He bowed and kowtowed twice.

sentences.zh: 又曰：「張璨不合加罪，望加敕赦之。

translations.literal: Again he said, "Zhang Can ought not receive added punishment; I hope Your Majesty will add an edict pardoning him.
translations.idiomatic: He added, "Zhang Can should not be punished further—I beg an edict of pardon.

sentences.zh: 」漢祖久之曰：「已行之矣。

translations.literal: " After a long while the Han founder said, "It has already been carried out.
translations.idiomatic: " After a long silence the emperor said, "It is already done.

sentences.zh: 」馮瀛王曰：「敕未下。

translations.literal: " Prince Feng of Ying said, "The edict has not been issued.
translations.idiomatic: " Feng said, "The decree has not yet gone out.

sentences.zh: 」漢祖遽曰：「與赦之。

translations.literal: " The Han founder hastily said, "Grant him pardon.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor said at once, "Then pardon him.

sentences.zh: 」馮曰：「勒停可乎？

translations.literal: " Feng said, "May it be ordered halted—would that suffice?
translations.idiomatic: " Feng asked, "May we simply halt the order?

sentences.zh: 」上曰：「可。

translations.literal: " The sovereign said, "It may be done.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor said, "Yes.

sentences.zh: 」由是改其敕，記其略曰：「三司邦計，國法攸依，張璨體事未明，執理乖當，宜停見職，犯牛皮者貸命放之。

translations.literal: " Thereupon the edict was revised, its summary recording: "The three departments govern the state's finances and national law depends on them; Zhang Can's grasp of affairs was unclear and his holding to principle was improper—he should cease his present office; those who violated cowhide are granted life and released.
translations.idiomatic: " The edict was rewritten along these lines: "The fiscal offices administer state revenue per national law. Zhang Can misunderstood the matter and argued unacceptably—remove him from office. The cowhide offenders are spared and released.

sentences.zh: 」大監聽宣敕訖，聞敕云「執理乖當」，尚曰：「中書自不能執理，若一一教外道判官執理，則焉用彼相乎！」）〉

translations.literal: " When the Director finished hearing the edict proclaimed, hearing the edict say "holding to principle improper," he still said, "The Secretariat itself cannot hold to principle—if one by one they teach borderland judges to hold to principle, then what use are those chancellors!" ) ]
translations.idiomatic: " After hearing the proclamation end with "argued unacceptably," Zhang still remarked, "If the Secretariat cannot uphold principle and must teach every provincial judge to do so, what good are those chancellors?") ]

sentences.zh: 乾祐中，道奉朝請外，平居自適。

translations.literal: In the Qianyou era Dao attended court outside the regular requests, living at ease in retirement.
translations.idiomatic: During the Qianyou reign Dao attended court only when summoned and lived quietly at leisure.

sentences.zh: 一日，著《長樂老自敘》云：

translations.literal: One day he composed An Old Man of Changle's Account of Himself, which reads:
translations.idiomatic: One day he wrote Account of an Old Man of Changle, which says:

sentences.zh: 余世家宗族，本始平、長樂二郡，歷代之名實，具載於國史家牒。

translations.literal: My family's clans for generations, rooted in the two commanderies Shiping and Changle—successive generations' names and deeds are fully recorded in the national histories and clan registers.
translations.idiomatic: My clan has roots in Shiping and Changle. The deeds of each generation are fully recorded in state histories and family registers.

sentences.zh: 余先自燕亡歸晉，事莊宗、明宗、閔帝、清泰帝，又事晉高祖皇帝、少帝。

translations.literal: I first fled Yan and returned to Jin, serving Zhuangzong, Mingzong, the Min emperor, and the Qingtai emperor, then also serving the Jin founding emperor and the minor emperor.
translations.idiomatic: I left Yan for Jin and served Zhuangzong, Mingzong, the Min emperor, and Emperor Qingtai, then the Jin founder and his successor.

sentences.zh: 契丹據汴京，為北主所制，自鎮州與文武臣僚、馬步將士歸漢朝，事高祖皇帝、今上。

translations.literal: When the Khitan held Bianjing, constrained by the northern ruler, from Zhenzhou with civil and military officials and infantry and cavalry commanders I returned to the Han court, serving the founding emperor and the present sovereign.
translations.idiomatic: When the Khitan held Bian, I was their captive until I left Zhenzhou with officials and troops for the Han court, serving the Han founder and the present emperor.

sentences.zh: 顧以久叨祿位，備歷艱危，上顯祖宗，下光親戚。

translations.literal: Considering that I have long enjoyed salary and rank, having borne every hardship, I display my ancestors above and bring glory to my kin below.
translations.idiomatic: Long enjoying rank and salary through every trial, I have honored my ancestors and brought credit to my kin.

sentences.zh: 亡曾祖諱湊，累贈至太傅，亡曾祖母崔氏，追封梁國太夫人；

translations.literal: My deceased great-grandfather, taboo name Cou, was repeatedly posthumously advanced to grand mentor; my deceased great-grandmother née Cui was posthumously ennobled as Grand Lady of Liang;
translations.idiomatic: My late great-grandfather Cou was posthumously advanced to grand mentor; my late great-grandmother, née Cui, was posthumously ennobled as Grand Lady of Liang;

sentences.zh: 亡祖諱炯，累贈至太師，亡祖母褚氏，追封吳國太夫人；

translations.literal: my deceased grandfather, taboo name Jiong, was repeatedly posthumously advanced to grand preceptor; my deceased grandmother née Chu was posthumously ennobled as Grand Lady of Wu;
translations.idiomatic: my late grandfather Jiong was posthumously advanced to grand preceptor; my late grandmother, née Chu, was posthumously ennobled as Grand Lady of Wu;

sentences.zh: 亡父諱良建，秘書少監致仕，累贈至尚書令，母張氏，追封魏國太夫人。

translations.literal: my deceased father, taboo name Liangjian, retired as vice director of the Secretariat, was repeatedly posthumously advanced to director of the Secretariat, and my mother née Zhang was posthumously ennobled as Grand Lady of Wei.
translations.idiomatic: my late father Liangjian, who retired as vice director of the Secretariat, was posthumously advanced to director of the Secretariat; my mother, née Zhang, was posthumously ennobled as Grand Lady of Wei.

sentences.zh: 余階自將仕郎，轉朝議郎、朝散大夫、銀青光祿大夫、金紫光祿大夫、特進、開府儀同三司。

translations.literal: My rank rose from gentleman for merit presentation, transferring to court deliberation gentleman, court dispersal grandee, silver-blue-gleam glory grandee, gold-purple-gleam glory grandee, specially advanced, and opening-office equal-to-three-departments.
translations.idiomatic: My rank rose from gentleman for merit presentation through court deliberation gentleman and court dispersal grandee, then silver and golden glory grandee titles, specially advanced status, to honorary commander equal to the Three Departments.

sentences.zh: 職自幽州節度巡官、河東節度巡官、掌書記，再為翰林學士，改授端明殿學士、集賢殿大學士、太微宮使，再為宏文館大學士，又充諸道鹽鐵轉運使、南郊大禮使、明宗皇帝晉高祖皇帝山陵使，再授定國軍節度、同州管內觀察處置等使，一為長春宮使，又授武勝軍節度、鄧隨均房等州管內觀察處置等使。

translations.literal: In office from circuit inspector of Youzhou military commission, circuit inspector of Hedong military commission, secretariat note-taker, twice as Hanlin academician, transferred to Duanming Hall academician, Jixian Hall great academician, Taiwei Palace commissioner, again as Hongwen Hall great academician, also served as salt and iron transport commissioner for all circuits, southern suburban grand ritual commissioner, mountain tomb commissioner for Emperors Mingzong and Jin founding emperor, again appointed military commissioner of Dingguo army and Tongzhou circuit observation and disposal commissioner, once as Changchun Palace commissioner, again appointed military commissioner of Wusheng army and Deng, Sui, Jun, Fang and other circuits' observation and disposal commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: My posts ran from Youzhou and Hedong circuit inspector to secretariat secretary, twice Hanlin academician, then Duanming and Jixian hall academician, Taiwei Palace commissioner, again Hongwen hall grand academician, also salt-and-iron transport commissioner for all circuits, commissioner for southern suburban rites and for the imperial tombs of Mingzong and the Jin founder, twice military commissioner of Dingguo and Tongzhou, once Changchun Palace commissioner, then military commissioner of Wusheng and observer of Deng, Sui, Jun, and Fang circuits.

sentences.zh: 官自攝幽府參軍、試大理評事、檢校尚書祠部郎中兼侍御史、檢校吏部郎中兼御史中丞、檢校太尉、同中書門下平章事、檢校太師、兼侍中，又授檢校太師、兼中書令。

translations.literal: In official title from acting You Prefecture staff officer, probationary grand court reviewer, investigating director of the Secretariat's ancestral temple office and concurrent palace censor, investigating director of the personnel office and concurrent censor-in-chief, investigating grand commandant, concurrent palace attendant and co-director of the Secretariat, investigating grand preceptor and concurrent director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: My offices ran from acting Youzhou staff officer and probationary grand court reviewer through investigating director of the ancestral temple office with concurrent palace censor, investigating personnel director with concurrent censor-in-chief, investigating grand commandant, concurrent palace attendant and co-director of the Secretariat, to investigating grand preceptor and director of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 正官自行臺中書舍人，再為戶部侍郎，轉兵部侍郎、中書侍郎，再為門下侍郎、刑部吏部尚書、右僕射，三為司空，兩在中書，一守本官，又授司徒、兼侍中，賜私門十六戟，又授太尉、兼侍中，又授戎太傅，又授漢太師。

translations.literal: In regular office from acting Secretariat drafter, twice as vice minister of revenue, transferred to vice minister of war and Secretariat vice director, again as vice director of the Secretariat, ministers of justice and personnel, right vice director, thrice as minister of works, twice in the Secretariat, once holding his original office, again appointed minister of education and concurrent palace attendant, granted sixteen halberds at his private gate, again appointed grand commandant and concurrent palace attendant, again appointed Khitan grand preceptor, again appointed Han grand preceptor.
translations.idiomatic: My regular posts ran from acting Secretariat drafter through twice vice minister of revenue, vice minister of war and Secretariat vice director, again vice director of the Secretariat, ministers of justice and personnel, right vice director, thrice minister of works with two terms in the Secretariat and one in his original office, then minister of education and palace attendant with sixteen halberds at his gate, grand commandant and palace attendant, Khitan grand preceptor, and Han grand preceptor.

sentences.zh: 爵自開國男至開國公、魯國公，再封秦國公、梁國公、燕國公、齊國公。

translations.literal: In noble rank from founding-state baron to founding-state duke, Duke of Lu, again enfeoffed Duke of Qin, Duke of Liang, Duke of Yan, and Duke of Qi.
translations.idiomatic: My titles ran from founding-state baron to founding-state duke, Duke of Lu, then Duke of Qin, Liang, Yan, and Qi.

sentences.zh: 食邑自三百戶至一萬一千戶，食實封自一百戶至一千八百戶。

translations.literal: Fief households from three hundred to eleven thousand; actual fief households from one hundred to one thousand eight hundred.
translations.idiomatic: My fief households rose from three hundred to eleven thousand; actual fief households from one hundred to eighteen hundred.

sentences.zh: 勛自柱國至上柱國。

translations.literal: Merit rank from pillar of state to supreme pillar of state.
translations.idiomatic: My merit rank rose from pillar of state to supreme pillar of state.

sentences.zh: 功臣名自經邦致理翊贊功臣至守正崇德保邦致理功臣、安時處順守義崇靜功臣、崇仁保德寧邦翊聖功臣。

translations.literal: Merit-lord names from merit lord who governs the realm and assists in support, to merit lord who upholds rectitude and exalts virtue, preserves the realm and governs it, merit lord who keeps time and attunes to order, upholds righteousness and reveres tranquillity, and merit lord who exalts benevolence, preserves virtue, pacifies the realm and assists the sage.
translations.idiomatic: My merit-lord titles ran from lord who governs the realm and assists the throne, to lord who upholds rectitude and exalts virtue while preserving the realm, lord who keeps peace and upholds righteousness, and lord who exalts benevolence, preserves virtue, pacifies the realm, and assists the sovereign.

sentences.zh: 先娶故德州戶掾褚諱濆女，早亡，後娶故景州弓高縣孫明府諱師禮女，累封蜀國夫人。

translations.literal: First I married the daughter of the late household registrar of De Prefecture, taboo name Fen, who died early; afterward I married the daughter of the late district magistrate of Gonggao in Jing Prefecture, taboo name Shili, who was repeatedly enfeoffed Lady of Shu.
translations.idiomatic: My first wife was the daughter of the late De Prefecture registrar Fen, who died young; my second wife was the daughter of the late Gonggao magistrate Shili of Jing Prefecture, ennobled as Lady of Shu.

sentences.zh: 亡長子平，自秘書郎授右拾遺、工部度支員外郎；

translations.literal: The deceased eldest son Ping, from Secretariat officer appointed right remonstrator and revenue bureau outer office member;
translations.idiomatic: My late eldest son Ping rose from Secretariat officer to right remonstrator and revenue bureau outer office member;

sentences.zh: 次子吉，自秘書省校書郎授膳部金部職方員外郎、屯田郎中；

translations.literal: the second son Ji, from secretariat collator appointed commissariat, treasury, and appointments outer office members and director of the garrison bureau;
translations.idiomatic: my second son Ji rose from secretariat collator to commissariat, treasury, and appointments outer office member and director of the garrison bureau;

sentences.zh: 第三亡子可，自秘書省正字授殿中丞、工部戶部員外郎；

translations.literal: the third deceased son Ke, from secretariat proofreader appointed palace director and works and revenue outer office members;
translations.idiomatic: my third son Ke, deceased, rose from secretariat proofreader to palace director and works and revenue outer office member;

sentences.zh: 第四子幼亡；

translations.literal: the fourth son died young;
translations.idiomatic: my fourth son died in childhood;

sentences.zh: 第五子義，自秘書郎改授銀青光祿大夫、檢校國子祭酒兼御史中丞，充定國軍衙內都指揮使，職罷改授朝散大夫、左春坊太子司議郎、授太常丞；

translations.literal: the fifth son Yi, from Secretariat officer transferred to silver-blue-gleam glory grandee, investigating director of the imperial academy and concurrent censor-in-chief, serving as inner commander of the Dingguo army, after leaving office transferred to court dispersal grandee, left spring palace crown prince petition reviewer, appointed grand director of sacrifices;
translations.idiomatic: my fifth son Yi rose from Secretariat officer to silver glory grandee, investigating director of the imperial academy with concurrent censor-in-chief, as inner commander of the Dingguo army, then after leaving office to court dispersal grandee, crown prince petition reviewer in the left spring palace, and grand director of sacrifices;

sentences.zh: 第六子正，自協律郎改授銀青光祿大夫、檢校國子祭酒兼御史中丞，充定國軍節度使，職罷改授朝散大夫、太僕丞。

translations.literal: the sixth son Zheng, from harmonizing-law officer transferred to silver-blue-gleam glory grandee, investigating director of the imperial academy and concurrent censor-in-chief, serving as military commissioner of the Dingguo army, after leaving office transferred to court dispersal grandee, grand director of the stud.
translations.idiomatic: my sixth son Zheng rose from harmonizing-law officer to silver glory grandee, investigating director of the imperial academy with concurrent censor-in-chief, as military commissioner of the Dingguo army, then after leaving office to court dispersal grandee and grand director of the stud.

sentences.zh: 長女適故兵部崔侍郎諱衍子太僕少卿名絢，封萬年縣君；

translations.literal: The eldest daughter married the son of the late vice minister of war Cui, taboo name Yan, named Xuan, grand director of the stud, enfeoffed Lady of Wannian;
translations.idiomatic: My eldest daughter married the son of the late Vice Minister Cui Yan, named Xuan, grand director of the stud, enfeoffed as Lady of Wannian;

sentences.zh: 三女子早亡。

translations.literal: three daughters died early.
translations.idiomatic: three daughters died young.

sentences.zh: 二孫幼亡。

translations.literal: Two grandsons died young.
translations.idiomatic: Two grandsons died in childhood.

sentences.zh: 唐長興二年敕，瀛州景城縣莊來蘇鄉改為元輔鄉，朝漢裏為孝行裏。

translations.literal: In the second year of Changxing of Tang, an edict changed the Zhuang of Ying Prefecture's Jingcheng county, Laisu township, to Yuanyu township, and Chaohan lane to Xiaoxing lane.
translations.idiomatic: In Tang Changxing year two an edict renamed Laisu township in Jingcheng, Yingzhou, to Yuanyu township and Chaohan lane to Xiaoxing lane.

sentences.zh: 洛南莊貫河南府洛陽縣三州鄉靈臺裏，奉晉天福五年敕，三州鄉改為上相鄉，靈臺裏改為中臺裏，時守司徒、兼侍中；

translations.literal: The Luonan estate spanned Sanzhou township and Lingtai lane of Luoyang county in Henan prefecture; following the Jin Tianfu fifth-year edict, Sanzhou township was changed to Shangxiang township and Lingtai lane to Zhongtai lane, at the time holding minister of education and concurrent palace attendant;
translations.idiomatic: My Luonan estate lay in Sanzhou township and Lingtai lane of Luoyang county, Henan; under the Jin Tianfu year-five edict Sanzhou became Shangxiang township and Lingtai became Zhongtai lane, while I held minister of education and palace attendant;

sentences.zh: 又奉八年敕，上相鄉改為太尉鄉，中臺裏改為侍中裏，時守太尉、兼侍中。

translations.literal: again following the eighth-year edict, Shangxiang township was changed to Grand Commandant township and Zhongtai lane to Palace Attendant lane, at the time holding grand commandant and concurrent palace attendant.
translations.idiomatic: under the year-eight edict Shangxiang became Grand Commandant township and Zhongtai became Palace Attendant lane, while I held grand commandant and palace attendant.

sentences.zh: 靜思本末，慶及存亡，蓋自國恩，盡從家法，承訓誨之旨，關教化之源，在孝於家，在忠於國，口無不道之言，門無不義之貨。

translations.literal: Reflecting quietly on root and branch, rejoicing that it reaches the living and the dead—this is all from national grace, all following family law, receiving the aim of instruction and teaching, touching the source of transformation: filial in the family, loyal in the state, the mouth without words not to be spoken, the gate without unrighteous goods.
translations.idiomatic: Reflecting on my life from beginning to end, I rejoice that honor reaches the living and the dead—all from imperial favor, all by family rule. I received my elders' teaching and hold to the source of moral transformation: filial at home, loyal in office, no improper word on my lips, no ill-gotten goods at my gate.

sentences.zh: 所願者下不欺於地，中不欺於人，上不欺於天，以三不欺為素。

translations.literal: What I desire is below not to deceive the earth, in the middle not to deceive men, above not to deceive Heaven—taking these three non-deceptions as my constant.
translations.idiomatic: I wish never to deceive earth below, men in the middle, or Heaven above—these three honesties are my standard.

sentences.zh: 賤如是，貴如是，長如是，老如是，事親、事君、事長、臨人之道，曠蒙天恕，累經難而獲多福，曾陷蕃而歸中華，非人之謀，是天之祐。

translations.literal: Base thus, noble thus, long thus, old thus—in the ways of serving parents, serving the ruler, serving elders, and facing men, broadly receiving Heaven's forgiveness, repeatedly passing through hardship yet obtaining many blessings, once falling into the barbarians yet returning to China—not by men's scheming, but by Heaven's aid.
translations.idiomatic: Humble or honored, young or old, in serving parents, ruler, elders, and subjects alike, I have been spared by Heaven through repeated trials and gained many blessings; I fell among barbarians yet returned to China—not by human design but by Heaven's grace.

sentences.zh: 六合之內有幸者，百歲之後有歸所。

translations.literal: Within the four seas there are the fortunate; after a hundred years there is a place to return.
translations.idiomatic: Those blessed within the realm have a home to return to after a hundred years.

sentences.zh: 無以珠玉含，當以時服斂，以籧篨葬，及擇不食之地而葬焉，以不及於古人故。

translations.literal: Do not place pearls and jade in the mouth; one should be enshrouded in seasonal dress, buried in a rush coffin, and choose land for burial that does not encroach on antiquity—because one cannot match the ancients.
translations.idiomatic: Do not fill my mouth with pearls and jade; bury me in seasonal dress in a plain rush coffin on unclaimed ground, for I cannot match the ancients.

sentences.zh: 祭以特羊，戒殺生也，當以不害命之物祭。

translations.literal: Sacrifice with a single ram; warn against killing living things—one should sacrifice with things that do not harm life.
translations.idiomatic: Offer a single ram in sacrifice and forbid killing; use offerings that take no life.

sentences.zh: 無立神道碑，以三代墳前不獲立碑故。

translations.literal: Do not erect a spirit-way stele, because in the Three Dynasties one might not erect steles before tombs.
translations.idiomatic: Erect no spirit-path stele, for the ancients of the Three Dynasties set no steles before their tombs.

sentences.zh: 無請謚號，以無德故。

translations.literal: Do not request a posthumous title, because there is no virtue.
translations.idiomatic: Seek no posthumous title, for I have no virtue to warrant one.

sentences.zh: 又念自賓佐至王佐及領藩鎮時，或有微益於國之事節，皆形於公籍。

translations.literal: Again, reflecting from aide to chief minister and when holding frontier commands, whenever there were slight benefits to the state in particulars, all were recorded in the public registers.
translations.idiomatic: I also recall that from staff officer to chief minister and as frontier commander, any small service to the state was recorded in official archives.

sentences.zh: 所著文章篇詠，因多事散失外，收拾得者，編於家集，其間見其志，知之者，罪之者，未知眾寡矣。

translations.literal: Essays and poems composed—because many affairs scattered them abroad, apart from what was gathered in, compiled in the family collection; among them those who see his intent, who know him, who blame him, I do not know whether they are many or few.
translations.idiomatic: My essays and poems, most lost in the turmoil, survive only in a family collection. How many readers understand my intent, know me, or condemn me, I cannot say.

sentences.zh: 有莊、有宅、有群書，有三子可以襲其業。

translations.literal: There are estates, dwellings, and collected books; there are three sons who can inherit the enterprise.
translations.idiomatic: I have estates, a home, a library, and three sons to carry on my work.

sentences.zh: 於此日五盥，日三省，尚猶日知其所亡，月無忘其所能。

translations.literal: On this day five washings, thrice daily self-examination—still one says daily he knows what he has lost, monthly he does not forget what he can do.
translations.idiomatic: Even now I bathe five times and examine myself thrice daily, still mindful that each day brings loss and each month tests what skill remains.

sentences.zh: 為子、為弟、為人臣、為師長、為夫、為父，有子、有猶子、有孫，奉身即有餘矣。

translations.literal: As son, as younger brother, as minister, as teacher and elder, as husband, as father, having sons, having nephew-sons, having grandsons—supporting the person, there is surplus.
translations.idiomatic: As son, brother, minister, teacher, husband, and father, with sons, nephews, and grandsons, I have done enough for myself.

sentences.zh: 為時乃不足，不足者何？

translations.literal: For the age, it is not enough; what is not enough?
translations.idiomatic: For the times, it is not enough—but what is lacking?

sentences.zh: 不能為大君致一統、定八方，誠有愧於歷職歷官，何以答乾坤之施。

translations.literal: I could not bring unity to the realm and settle the eight directions for my great lord—truly I feel shame before the offices I have held; how could I repay Heaven and Earth's gifts?
translations.idiomatic: I failed to bring unity to the realm and secure the eight directions for my sovereign—I am ashamed before every office I have held. How could I repay what Heaven and Earth have given me?

sentences.zh: 時開一卷，時飲一杯，食味別聲、被色，老安於當代耶！

translations.literal: From time to time I open a scroll, from time to time I drink a cup—savoring flavors, distinguishing sounds, draped in colors—growing old at ease in the present age!
translations.idiomatic: Now and then I open a book, now and then I raise a cup—tasting flavors, hearing music, wrapped in color—growing old at peace in my own time!

sentences.zh: 老而自樂，何樂如之！

translations.literal: To grow old and find joy in oneself—what joy could surpass this!
translations.idiomatic: To grow old and be content with oneself—what greater joy could there be!

sentences.zh: 時乾祐三年朱明月長樂老序云。

translations.literal: Thus ends the preface to the Old Man of Changle, dated the third year of Qianyou, on the fifteenth day of the first month, by Zhu Mingyue.
translations.idiomatic: So concludes the preface to the Old Man of Changle, written in the third year of Qianyou by Zhu Mingyue.

sentences.zh: 及太祖平內難，議立徐州節度使劉赟為漢嗣，遣道與秘書監趙上交、樞密直學士王度等往迎之。

translations.literal: When the Taizu pacified the internal crisis, the court resolved to install Liu Yun, military governor of Xuzhou, as heir to Han, and sent Dao together with Director of the Secretariat Zhao Shangjiao, Privy Council academician Wang Du, and others to welcome him.
translations.idiomatic: When Taizu quelled the internal crisis, the court decided to make Liu Yun, military governor of Xuzhou, heir to the Han throne and sent Dao with Zhao Shangjiao, director of the secretariat, Wang Du, privy council academician, and others to escort him to the capital.

sentences.zh: 道尋與赟自徐赴汴，行至宋州，會澶州軍變。

translations.literal: Dao soon accompanied Yun from Xuzhou toward Bian, and when they reached Song Prefecture they encountered the army mutiny at Dazhou.
translations.idiomatic: Dao soon set out with Yun from Xuzhou toward Bianjing, but at Song Prefecture they ran into the mutiny of the Dazhou garrison.

sentences.zh: 樞密使王峻遣郭崇領兵至，屯於衙門外，時道與上交等宿於衙內。

translations.literal: Privy Council commissioner Wang Jun sent Guo Chong with troops, who encamped outside the headquarters gate while Dao and Shangjiao and the others lodged inside.
translations.idiomatic: Privy council commissioner Wang Jun sent Guo Chong with troops, who camped outside the headquarters gate while Dao, Shangjiao, and the rest stayed inside.

sentences.zh: 是日，赟率左右甲士闔門登樓，詰崇所自，崇言太祖已副推戴。

translations.literal: That day Yun led his armored guards to shut the gate and ascend the tower, demanding where Chong had come from. Chong said the Taizu had already been acclaimed by popular assent.
