translations.idiomatic: That day Yun led his armored guards to bar the gate and climb the tower, demanding Chong's purpose. Chong replied that Taizu had already been acclaimed by the army.

sentences.zh: 左右知其事變，以為道所賣，皆欲殺道等以自快。

translations.literal: His attendants, learning of the turn of events, believed Dao had betrayed them and all wished to kill Dao and the others to vent their rage.
translations.idiomatic: Yun's men, seeing how events had turned, believed Dao had sold them out and wanted to kill Dao and his companions on the spot.

sentences.zh: 趙上交與王度聞之，皆惶怖不知所為，惟道偃仰自適，略無懼色，尋亦獲免焉。

translations.literal: Zhao Shangjiao and Wang Du, hearing of it, were both terrified and did not know what to do, but only Dao reclined at ease without the slightest sign of fear, and before long he too was spared.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Shangjiao and Wang Du were both terrified and at a loss, but Dao alone lay back at ease without a trace of fear, and before long he too was spared.

sentences.zh: 道微時嘗賦詩云：「終聞海嶽歸明主，未省乾坤陷吉人。

translations.literal: In his youth Dao once composed a poem that said, "In the end I hear that seas and mountains return to a bright lord; I have never seen Heaven and Earth trap a man of fortune."
translations.idiomatic: In his youth Dao had written a poem: "In the end the seas and mountains return to a worthy sovereign; I have never known Heaven and Earth to destroy a man of fortune."

sentences.zh: 」至是其言驗矣。

translations.literal: Now his words were fulfilled.
translations.idiomatic: Now his words had come true.

sentences.zh: （《青箱雜記》載馮道詩全篇云：莫為危時便愴神，前程往往有期因，終聞海嶽歸明主，未省乾坤陷吉人。

translations.literal: (The Qingxiang Zaji records Feng Dao's complete poem as follows: Do not let perilous times break your spirit; the road ahead often has its appointed cause. In the end I hear that seas and mountains return to a bright lord; I have never seen Heaven and Earth trap a man of fortune.
translations.idiomatic: (The Qingxiang Zaji gives Feng Dao's poem in full: Do not let hard times break your spirit—the road ahead often has its reason. In the end the seas and mountains return to a worthy sovereign; I have never known Heaven and Earth to destroy a man of fortune.

sentences.zh: 道德幾時曾去世，舟車何處不通津，但教方寸無諸惡，狼虎叢中也立身。）〉

translations.literal: When has virtue ever left the world? Where do boats and carts not find a ford? Only teach your heart to harbor no evil, and you may stand upright even in a pack of wolves and tigers.)〉
translations.idiomatic: When has virtue ever left the world? Where do boats and carts not find a crossing? Keep your heart free of evil, and you may stand upright even among wolves and tigers.)〉

sentences.zh: 廣順初，復拜太師、中書令，太祖甚重之，每進對不以名呼。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Guangshun era he was again appointed grand preceptor and director of the secretariat. The Taizu valued him greatly and whenever he came to audience never addressed him by name.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Guangshun reign he was again made grand preceptor and director of the secretariat. Taizu held him in the highest regard and never addressed him by name in audience.

sentences.zh: 及太祖崩，世宗以道為山陵使。

translations.literal: When the Taizu died, Shizong appointed Dao commissioner for the imperial tomb.
translations.idiomatic: When Taizu died, Shizong appointed Dao commissioner for the imperial tomb.

sentences.zh: 會河東劉崇入寇，世宗召大臣議欲親征，道諫止之，世宗因言：「唐初，天下草寇蜂起，並是太宗親平之。

translations.literal: When Liu Chong of Hedong invaded, Shizong summoned the chief ministers to discuss a personal campaign. Dao remonstrated and stopped it. Shizong then said, "In early Tang, bandits rose everywhere across the realm, and it was Taizong who personally pacified them all."
translations.idiomatic: When Liu Chong of Hedong invaded, Shizong called the chief ministers to discuss leading the campaign in person. Dao dissuaded him. Shizong then said, "In early Tang, rebels swarmed across the land, and it was Taizong who put them down himself."

sentences.zh: 」道奏曰：「陛下得如太宗否？

translations.literal: Dao submitted, "Can Your Majesty match Taizong?"
translations.idiomatic: Dao replied, "Can Your Majesty match Taizong?"

sentences.zh: 」世宗怒曰：「馮道何相少也！

translations.literal: Shizong said angrily, "How Feng Dao underestimates me!"
translations.idiomatic: Shizong snapped, "How little Feng Dao thinks of me!"

sentences.zh: 」乃罷。

translations.literal: The discussion ended.
translations.idiomatic: The discussion ended there.

sentences.zh: 及世宗親征，不及扈從，留道奉太祖山陵。

translations.literal: When Shizong campaigned in person, Dao could not accompany him and was left behind to oversee the Taizu's tomb.
translations.idiomatic: When Shizong marched in person, Dao could not accompany him and was left to oversee Taizu's tomb.

sentences.zh: 時道已抱疾。

translations.literal: By then Dao was already ill.
translations.idiomatic: By then Dao was already gravely ill.

sentences.zh: 及山陵禮畢，奉神主歸舊宮，未及祔廟，一夕薨於其第，時顯德元年四月十七日也，享年七十有三。

translations.literal: When the tomb rites were finished and the spirit tablet was brought back to the old palace, before it could be installed in the ancestral temple he died one night at his residence. It was the seventeenth day of the fourth month of the first year of Xiande; he was seventy-three.
translations.idiomatic: When the tomb rites were complete and the spirit tablet had been returned to the old palace but before it could be installed in the ancestral temple, he died in his home one night—the seventeenth day of the fourth month of the first year of Xiande, at the age of seventy-three.

sentences.zh: 世宗聞之，輟視朝三日，冊贈尚書令，追封瀛王，謚曰文懿。

translations.literal: When Shizong heard of it he suspended court audiences for three days, posthumously enfeoffed him as director of the secretariat, posthumously created him Prince of Ying, and gave him the posthumous title Wényì.
translations.idiomatic: Shizong suspended court for three days, posthumously appointed him director of the secretariat, created him Prince of Ying, and gave him the posthumous title Wényì, "Refined and Excellent."

sentences.zh: 道歷任四朝，三入中書，在相位二十餘年，以持重鎮俗為己任，未嘗以片簡擾於諸侯，平生甚廉儉。

translations.literal: Dao served four dynasties, entered the secretariat three times, and held the chancellorship for more than twenty years. He took steadying the customs as his charge, never troubled the regional lords with a single note, and throughout his life was very frugal.
translations.idiomatic: Dao served four dynasties, entered the secretariat three times, and held the chancellorship for more than twenty years. He made it his task to steady the realm through weight and restraint, never troubled a single regional lord with a private note, and lived his life in notable frugality.

sentences.zh: 逮至末年，閨庭之內，稍徇奢靡，其子吉，尤恣狂蕩，道不能制，識者以其不終令譽，鹹嘆惜之。

translations.literal: By his last years, within the household he indulged somewhat in luxury. His son Ji was especially unrestrained and dissolute; Dao could not control him. Men of discernment, seeing that his fine reputation would not last to the end, all sighed in regret.
translations.idiomatic: In his last years his household grew somewhat extravagant. His son Ji was especially wild and unrestrained, and Dao could not rein him in. Those who knew him sighed that his fine reputation would not endure to the end.

sentences.zh: （《五代史補》：馮道之鎮同州也，有酒務吏乞以家財修夫子廟，道以狀付判官參詳其事。

translations.literal: (The Wudai Shibu's supplement records: When Feng Dao governed Tong Prefecture, a wine-tax clerk petitioned to repair the Confucius temple at his own expense. Dao handed the petition to the judge for review.
translations.idiomatic: (The supplement to the History of the Five Dynasties records: When Feng Dao was posted to Tongzhou, a wine-tax clerk asked to repair the Confucius temple at his own expense. Dao referred the petition to his judge for review.

sentences.zh: 判官素滑稽，因以一絕書判後云：「荊棘森森繞杏壇，儒官高貴盡偷安，若教酒務修夫子，覺我慚惶也大難。

translations.literal: The judge, who was by nature a wit, appended a quatrain to his ruling: "Thorns and brambles thickly ring the apricot altar; lofty Confucian officers all steal their ease. If the wine-tax office is to repair the Master, I feel my shame would be beyond bearing."
translations.idiomatic: The judge, a born wit, appended a quatrain to his ruling: "Thorns and brambles ring the apricot altar round; lofty Confucian officers all steal their ease. If the wine-tax office must repair the Master, my shame would be more than I could bear."

sentences.zh: 」道覽之有愧色，因出俸重創之。

translations.literal: " Dao, reading it, showed a look of shame and therefore contributed from his salary to rebuild it properly.
translations.idiomatic: Dao read it and flushed with shame, then paid from his own salary to rebuild the temple properly.

sentences.zh: 馮瀛王道之在中書也，有舉子李導投贄所業，馮相見之，戲謂曰：「老夫名道，其來久矣，加以累居相府，秀才不可謂不知，然亦名導，於禮可乎？

translations.literal: When Prince Feng of Ying was at the secretariat, a candidate named Li Dao presented his work. The Feng chancellor received him and joked, "This old man's name is Dao and has been so a long time. Add to that repeated tenure in the chief minister's office—a young scholar cannot claim not to know it. Yet you too are named Dao—is that proper in ritual?"
translations.idiomatic: When Prince Feng of Ying was at the secretariat, a candidate named Li Dao presented his writings. The chancellor received him and teased, "My name is Dao and has been for a long time, and I have sat in the chief minister's office again and again—you cannot claim not to know it. Yet you are also named Dao—is that proper?"

sentences.zh: 」李抗聲對曰：「相公是無寸底道字，小子有寸底導字，何謂不可也！

translations.literal: " Li answered loudly, "The chancellor's character Dao has no inch at the bottom; this young man's character Dao has an inch at the bottom—how could it be improper!"
translations.idiomatic: Li answered boldly, "Your character Dao has no 'inch' at the bottom; mine has an 'inch' at the bottom—what could be improper about that!"

sentences.zh: 」公笑曰：「老夫不惟名無寸，諸事亦無寸，吾子可謂知人矣。

translations.literal: " The prince laughed and said, "This old man not only has no inch in his name—he has no inch in anything. Young man, you may be called one who knows people."
translations.idiomatic: The prince laughed and said, "I have no inch not only in my name but in anything I do. Young man, you know your man."

sentences.zh: 」了無怒色。

translations.literal: " He showed not the slightest anger.
translations.idiomatic: He showed not a trace of anger.

sentences.zh: 馮吉，瀛王道之子，能彈琵琶，以皮為弦，世宗嘗令彈於御前，深欣善之，因號其琵琶曰「繞殿雷」也。

translations.literal: Feng Ji, son of Prince Feng of Ying, could play the pipa with leather strings. Shizong once ordered him to perform before the throne and was deeply pleased, and therefore named his pipa "Thunder Rolling Round the Hall."
translations.idiomatic: Feng Ji, son of Prince Feng of Ying, played the pipa with leather strings. Shizong once had him perform before the throne and was so delighted that he named the instrument "Thunder Rolling Round the Hall."

sentences.zh: 道以其惰業，每加譴責，而吉攻之愈精，道益怒，凡與客飲，必使庭立而彈之，曲罷或賜以束帛，命背負之，然後致謝。

translations.literal: Dao, because of his lazy pursuits, often rebuked him, but Ji practiced all the more diligently, which only angered Dao further. Whenever he drank with guests he made Ji stand in the courtyard and play; when the piece ended he sometimes bestowed a bundle of silk and ordered him to carry it on his back before he might give thanks.
translations.idiomatic: Dao rebuked him constantly for his idle pursuits, but Ji only practiced harder, which made Dao angrier still. Whenever he entertained guests he made Ji stand in the courtyard and play; when the piece ended he sometimes gave him a bundle of silk and made him carry it on his back before he was allowed to bow his thanks.

sentences.zh: 道自以為戒勖極矣，吉未能悛改，既而益自若。

translations.literal: Dao thought he had disciplined him to the utmost, but Ji could not reform and afterward grew only more self-assured.
translations.idiomatic: Dao thought he had disciplined him as far as possible, but Ji would not change and only grew more brazen.

sentences.zh: 道度無可奈何，嘆曰：「百工之司藝而身賤，理使然也。

translations.literal: Dao, seeing nothing more he could do, sighed and said, "Among the hundred crafts, those who master an art remain base in station—it is the way of things."
translations.idiomatic: Dao, seeing nothing more to be done, sighed and said, "Among the hundred crafts, mastery of an art still leaves a man low in rank—that is how things are."

sentences.zh: 此子不過太常少卿耳。

translations.literal: This boy will rise no higher than vice director of the court of imperial sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: This boy will never rise above vice director of the court of imperial sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 」其後果終於此。）〉

translations.literal: " In the end he indeed finished his career at that post.)〉
translations.idiomatic: In the end that is exactly where he finished.)〉

sentences.zh: 史臣曰：道之履行，郁有古人之風；

translations.literal: The historiographer says: In conduct and deportment, Dao had the dense fragrance of ancient style;
translations.idiomatic: The historiographer writes: In conduct and bearing, Dao had something of the ancients about him;

sentences.zh: 道之宇量，深得大臣之禮。

translations.literal: in breadth of spirit he deeply embodied the rites of a great minister.
translations.idiomatic: in breadth of spirit he deeply embodied what a great minister should be.

sentences.zh: 然而事四朝，相六帝，可得為忠乎！

translations.literal: Yet having served four dynasties and been chief minister to six emperors—can this be called loyalty!
translations.idiomatic: Yet he served four dynasties and was chief minister to six emperors—can that be called loyalty!

sentences.zh: 夫一女二夫，人之不幸，況於再三者哉！

translations.literal: For a woman to have two husbands is a person's misfortune—how much more when it happens a third time!
translations.idiomatic: For a woman to have two husbands is misfortune enough—how much worse when it happens again and again!

sentences.zh: 所以飾終之典，不得謚為文貞、文忠者，蓋謂此也。

translations.literal: That is why in the rites of his funeral he could not receive the posthumous titles Wénzhēn or Wénzhōng.
translations.idiomatic: That is why the funeral honors could not include the posthumous titles Wénzhēn or Wénzhōng—"Refined and Upright" or "Refined and Loyal."
